answer:
Use OpenFOAM with the interFoam solver to model gravity-driven sloshing in a partially filled rectangular tank.
The tank is a rectangular box 1.0 m long in x, 0.6 m tall in y, and 0.1 m deep in z.
Run the case as a transient simulation with gravity g = (0 -9.81 0).
Use one of two mesh options: a 2D setup with blockMesh 200 x 120 x 1 cells and front/back patches in z set as empty, or a fully 3D setup with 200 x 120 x 20 cells.
For the baseline run use the 2D setup (200 x 120 x 1 with empty frontAndBack patches); all other settings remain identical if switching to the 3D mesh.
The tank is stationary with fixed walls; sloshing is initiated solely by an initial tilt of the free surface, with no prescribed tank motion or forcing.
Initialize water with a tilted free surface whose depth varies linearly from 0.25 m at x=0 to 0.35 m at x=1.0.
Build the initial condition in setFields as a staircase approximation using 10 x-slices, each 0.1 m wide, with water heights following the linear ramp (e.g., 0.255 m at the first slice, rising by 0.01 m per slice up to 0.345 m in the last slice).
In each slice, set alpha.water = 1 from y=0 up to the slice height; everywhere else alpha.water = 0.
Initialize the velocity field to U = (0 0 0) and p_rgh = 0.
Treat the flow as laminar with no turbulence model (simulationType laminar in constant/turbulenceProperties).
Use water with density 1000 kg/m3 and kinematic viscosity 1e-06 m2/s, and air with density 1 kg/m3 and kinematic viscosity 1.48e-05 m2/s, both Newtonian.
Set the surface tension coefficient sigma to 0.07 N/m in constant/physicalProperties.
Apply noSlip for U, fixedFluxPressure for p_rgh, and zeroGradient for alpha.water on the left, right, and bottom walls.
At the open top boundary (y = 0.6 m), apply pressureInletOutletVelocity for U, totalPressure with p0 = 0 for p_rgh, and inletOutlet for alpha.water with inletValue 0.
Run the simulation to endTime 10 s with adjustTimeStep enabled, maxCo 0.5, an initial deltaT of 1e-3 s, and write output every 0.05 s.
